restrictions: Classical probabilistic 256-bit word RAM under collision-frontier-v5 (C = 2224); total work over all processors, including construction of the exact published starting solution (charged at 2^35 = 34,359,738,368 units) and the statically audited 2^32-bucket table build plus the lane-packed P4 copy (at most 23,035,438,979 units, itemised audit), both in preprocessing. The published Fig. 6 characteristic is public algorithm text and its historical discovery is not charged (public-characteristic); charging the measured re-derivation (32 x 593,858 CPU-s at 2^23 units = 159,412,543,029,248 units) would give 2^47.1947.

Two-block messages M0||M1 and M0||M1' of 128 bytes; complete SHA-256 with standard IV, steps 0..31 on all three padded blocks, feed-forward and all 256 digest bits; outputs verified by full recomputation and accompanied by a verified 128-byte 32-step collision certificate.

32-step truncation of the 35-step attack of Li, Liu, Wang, Shi (CRYPTO 2026, ePrint 2026/1080), using its Fig. 6 characteristic as public algorithm text and its starting solution as charged advice; truncation, table and Step-2/3 tests follow hash-smash #26/#33 (winglock), re-implemented and re-measured in #296 (mitchuski), with the certified 32-step witness and deterministic compact-table slice replay from #227 (yudduy). On organizer-generated inputs, the replay checks one witness lineage and bit-exact equivalence and primitive operation counts (Swar7Counter) of its 7-lane 36-bit guard-bit SWAR C_32 evaluator against seven scalar evaluations, the charged 64-register program (Reg64: lanes against scalar C_32, arithmetic and traffic counts, peak liveness <= 64) and the lazy CV1 extraction; it does not validate the current 32-bit-bucket table cardinalities, completeness, build cost or full-run resource bound.

One run of T = 7,832,802,607,654 independent uniform first-block trials in B_7 = ceil(T/7) = 1,118,971,801,094 7-lane 36-bit guard-bit SWAR batches on the 256-bit word RAM with 64 registers (register-machine-64) at 2,273 operations per batch: 2,047 arithmetic (32 rand+mask, 464 schedule with merged sigma masks, 1,521 optimised rounds of 6e5214dd, 16 feed-forward, 14 for CV1[0]), 202 traffic (71 loads; 30 stores, M0 included; 101 address) and 24 entry/exit, asserted by the replay's Reg64 program (liveness 53 + 8 persistent <= 64). CV1[1..7] of a lane are extracted only for a nonempty-bucket trial (56 operations in the capped work). Another 32 operations (31 itemised) per used trial cover the 2^32-bucket lookup, under the Step-2/3 cap 96.2 T. Step 3 sweeps stages 16-17 seven candidates per word as in f807117b. Unused slots of the final batch are charged; no restarts.

The full product of the declared per-trial lower-bound factors and one-sided Bernstein (excess 3.277 T over E[X] <= 92.923, E[X^2] <= 4.2301e12, support 435,642,196,448) gives cap-stop probability < 1.3145e-4 and success > 0.395000. Exact integer ceilings total 1,652,533,755,683 units (A+B < 1,595,138,578,336; C <= 23,035,438,979; D = 2^35), log2 = 40.5878168800 < 40.588; preprocessing 57,395,177,347 < 2^35.7403. Base: passed 6e5214dd (Meganpark980320, 42.745) on f807117b, d8d39011, 621d0fb0 and Th0rgal's f310d44f. Ours: the corrected Step-3 count 2^-44 (measured p_L = 2^-44.0055 charged, success >= 0.395); the batch on the declared 64-register machine (register-machine-64) with merged sigma masks and an itemised reserve, lazy CV1[1..7] extraction, itemised table-build audit; cap and T re-optimised. With 6e5214dd's register use the total would be 2^40.714717.

Conditional-selection premise: V counts accepted TAB2 record occurrences. Conditionally on V >= 1, an analysis-only auxiliary seed sampled independently after the trial chooses J uniformly from those V occurrences. The declared selected-valid-tuple-success-transfer heuristic gives Pr[Step3(J) succeeds | V >= 1] >= r = 196,608 p_L (1 - U/2) >= 1.113314e-8 (step3-44-conditions). The counterfactual uncapped trial tests every occurrence, so success through J implies uncapped-trial success; the cap is then handled separately by a union bound.

Heuristic bound: relies on public-characteristic, q-32step-matching-rate, step3-44-conditions, cv1-conditional-uniformity, selected-valid-tuple-success-transfer, register-machine-64, attack-work-moments, precomputation-op-cap, valid-tuple-pairs and starting-solution-cost (score-critical), plus route-search-measured, cpu-second-pricing (fallback only) and search-peak-memory (supporting).

heuristics.statement: The published signed characteristic of Li, Liu, Wang and Shi (CRYPTO 2026, Fig. 6), as truncated to 32 steps in public hash-smash #26/#33, and its two-bit conditions under the stated readings are public algorithm text that the algorithm may use without charging their original discovery. They are a table of conditions, not a collision, and contain no message word, chaining value or state value.
heuristics.scope: The signed rows and two-bit conditions only. Every value-level object (the starting solution, tables P1-P4, first blocks, valid tuples, second blocks) is computed and charged: D = 2^35, C <= 23,035,438,979 units, and the online work A + B (proof Sections 4, 8).
heuristics.extrapolation: The characteristic is printed in the cited publication and restated in proof Section 2; the authors' search model is public (Peace9911/sha_2_attack), and #396's completed re-run of S's procedure returned exactly these signed rows. The organizer-accepted SHA-256 r31 package 50592e75 (heuristic H1-public-characteristic) uses the same convention for the published 31-step characteristic. The cost model's omitted-search rule is honoured for every value-level object (proof Section 6.1); the characteristic is stored within the 2^13-byte advice bound.
heuristics.limitations: The historical discovery cost of the characteristic is not charged. If a reviewer charged the measured re-derivation (32 x 593,858 CPU-s at 2^23), the total of this version would be 2^47.1946370415 (f310d44f claimed 2^47.2721673216 with the same E); with no rediscovery factor, 2^42.5931.

heuristics.statement: A uniform first block M0 compressed with C_32 from the IV yields at least 2^-17.3584 expected valid tuple occurrences (accepted TAB2 records in Step 2) against TAB2 of 1,396,774,912 records.
heuristics.scope: The exact TAB2 and Step-2 tests of proof Section 4 with C_32 first blocks.
heuristics.extrapolation: Exact-enumeration prediction 2^-17.3254; four measured runs, 2^34 part-trials and 25,936 valid tuples give pooled q_hat = 25,936/2^32 = 2^-17.3373. A one-sided normal approximation to the summed rare-event counts gives the 99% lower bound (25,936 - 2.32635 sqrt(25,936))/2^32 = 2^-17.3583236, rounded downward here to 2^-17.3584. The retained tuple slice replay verifies one fixed derivation but does not estimate q.
heuristics.limitations: Large-scale rate runs are participant C executions; treats CV1 words as uniform for the Step-2 tests.

heuristics.statement: For a valid tuple drawn from the pooled accepted TAB2 record occurrences of fresh uniform trials (occurrence-weighted), each of its 196,608 P4 candidates passes Step-3 stages 16..31 with probability at least p_L = 2^-44.0055 on average, and the expected number of other passing candidates of the same tuple given that one passes is at most 0.0000361053. Hence the tuple's Step-3 success probability is at least r = 196,608 p_L (1 - U/2) with U/2 < 2^-15.75, i.e. r >= 1.113314e-8.
heuristics.scope: Stages 16..31 of the real two-sided second block with the real P4 list, the fixed advice and the exact Step-3 tests of proof Section 4, for the occurrence-weighted valid-tuple distribution; W16..W19 enter through their law under cv1-conditional-uniformity; the validity weights and tuple vectors assume CV1[1..3] uniform given CV1[0], the premise already declared in q-32step-matching-rate. Replaces step3-46-conditions: the 46-count included the printed relation W20[4,31] = W20[6,22], which the published pair violates, the algorithm never tests and the 32-step route does not require.
heuristics.extrapolation: Corrected count (proof Section 5.1): 44 one-bit conditions, at stages 16..31 3, 12, 6, 7, 4, 1, 8, 3; the late conditions (stages 20..31) are derived algebraically from the XOR-linearity of sigma1 and match the printed W20/W22 relations except the misprint. Pre-registered measurement (proof Section 5.1, Appendix F): 8 key slices of the exactly rebuilt TAB2, 1,573 records examined and 700 with nonzero validity weight, 1,400 tuple vectors, 30 batches, 73,231,079 histories through step 19; occurrence-weighted p = 2^-44.0004, 99% bounds [2^-44.0055, 2^-43.9954] (outer of t and two-way bootstrap); stage exponents 3.0000, 11.9998, 6.0001, 7.0003, 4.0003, 1.0000, 7.9993, 3.0005; every counted condition enforced from its stage and at 0.5 before it; no heterogeneity by vector, record, slice, class size or weight; replication 2^-44.0029; 200 of 200 dumped passes completed into real 32-step collisions. Co-pass: 520,582 pass events, 99% upper bound 3.61e-5 on the size-biased co-pass mean; no independence formula is used.
heuristics.limitations: The measurement is a participant run with our own tools, not an organizer execution (not feasible within the executor's limits). The rate is measured on simulated second-block histories whose law rests on cv1-conditional-uniformity. Records come from 8 of 256 key slices and a 2^-10 sub-sample; transfer to all of TAB2 assumes representativeness, which the slice and class-size tests support but cannot prove. The independence of the 44 conditions is not proved; the bound charges the measured lower bound, not the count. The success bound stays >= 0.39 down to p = 2^-44.0293 (1.6% below p_L); at p = 2^-44.5 it would be 0.2999.

heuristics.statement: For a uniform first block M0 and CV1 = C_32(IV, M0), conditionally on the Step-2 validity events of the trial's TAB2 records (which records are valid, hence V), CV1[4..7] is, to the precision used, uniform on 2^128 and independent of those events. Consequently W0..W3 and W16..W19 of every valid tuple have the uniform law, independent of the trial's Step-2 events and the tuple's W4..W15, that the simulator of proof Section 5.1 uses.
heuristics.scope: Only the law of CV1[4..7] given CV1[0..3]-measurable events, as used by the reduction of proof Section 5.1 (b)-(c): the law of W16..W19 for valid tuples, hence the transfer of the simulated Step-3 rate to real valid tuples.
heuristics.extrapolation: W0..W3 and W16..W19 are triangular bijections of CV1[4..7] given CV1[0..3] and the tuple (proof Section 5.1). The q premise already treats CV1 words as uniform, and the measured q agrees with the exact-enumeration prediction that assumes uniform CV1[0..3] (2^-17.3373 measured, 2^-17.3254 predicted). #296's stage rates on real trials, where W16..W19 come from the real CV1[4..7] of real valid tuples (2^-3.000, 2^-15.000, 2^-21.03 and 2^-27.79 through stages 16..19), agree with the simulator's rates under uniform W16..W19 (2^-3, 2^-15, 2^-21, 2^-28.0002).
heuristics.limitations: Not proved: C_32 is a fixed function, and its output words are not exactly independent. The evidence is agreement of real-trial rates with uniform-input predictions, at the precision of those campaigns (about 1% for q and stages 16-17, 21% for stage 19 with 22 events). #296's stage 20 shows 5 of 22 stage-19 survivors passing against about 1.4 expected; candidates of one W14 group share W20, so passes cluster, and 22 events cannot resolve this. The premise is an approximation for a fixed function, not exact for arbitrary small events.

heuristics.statement: For a fresh uniform first-block trial conditioned on V >= 1 accepted TAB2 record occurrences, let an analysis-only auxiliary seed sampled independently after the trial choose J uniformly from those V occurrences. The conditional probability that Step 3 on J contains at least one fully conforming P4 candidate is at least r = 196,608 p_L (1 - U/2) >= 1.113314e-8 (step3-44-conditions).
heuristics.scope: The fixed submitted TAB2 and P4, exact Step-2 test and Step-3 test over fresh independent uniform first blocks. J is an analysis-only uniform selector over accepted record occurrences and adds no coins or work to the submitted algorithm. The counterfactual uncapped trial tests every occurrence, so success through J is contained in uncapped-trial success; the cap is handled separately.
heuristics.extrapolation: The corrected count and the occurrence-weighted measurement (proof Section 5.1) supply r for the occurrence-weighted tuple; across tuples E[p_J^2]/p^2 <= 1.0044 (99%). From E[C(V,2)] <= q/32 and Pr[V>=1] >= 31q/32, at most 1/31 of nonempty trials have V>=2; also E[V 1_{V>=2}] <= 2E[C(V,2)] <= q/16, so at least 15/16 of occurrence mass comes from singleton trials where the two selectors coincide. This is relevance evidence only: the declared transfer still assumes that conditioning on V>=1 and changing to a trial-first, then uniform-within-trial selector do not reduce Step-3 success below r.
heuristics.limitations: No participant campaign reports Step-3 outcomes stratified by V or compares occurrence-weighted with trial-weighted uniform-tuple rates, and no complete late-stage pass occurred in the rate campaign. The pair bound does not exclude concentration of the very rare Step-3 successes in multi-tuple trials; multiplicity and success may be correlated. The certified witness proves feasibility only; if this conditional transfer fails, the 0.39 success claim is unsupported.

heuristics.statement: Fallback only, not in the claimed total: Constructing the published 35-step characteristic, given its nabla W as part of the advice, costs at most 32 times the solver CPU time of the measured run of S's procedure (M_E = 593,858 CPU-seconds); the charged upper bound is exactly 159,412,543,029,248 < 2^47.179759 target-compression units at 2^23 units per CPU-second.
heuristics.scope: Fallback only: the characteristic search, if a reviewer charges it (proof Section 6.2). Not part of the claimed total; its memory is declared under search-peak-memory.
heuristics.extrapolation: The public PR #396 run executed S's four-step procedure with the authors' model library until a Step-4 call at threshold 76 returned a characteristic equal to Fig. 6 in every signed row; all 59 calls and 593,858 CPU-seconds are charged. The factor 32 is an itemised blind-rediscovery factor of about 8 (priced from its timed-out blind descent and three tA levels) times a residual factor 4 (solver variance and exploratory-model/nabla-W choice).
heuristics.limitations: Steps 2-4 were conditioned on S's nabla W, and Step 4 targeted S's published thresholds rather than completing a blind descent; 76 was reached but not proved optimal. The x32 margin prices blind rediscovery from the run ledger but was not itself executed, and S's historical time is unpublished. Enters only the fallback total 2^47.1946370415 for a reviewer who charges the characteristic search (proof Section 6.2).

heuristics.statement: Fallback only, not in the claimed total: One solver CPU-second on the measurement machine costs at most 2^23 target-compression units (2^34.12 primitive 256-bit word-RAM operations, 17.0 operations per retired instruction).
heuristics.scope: Fallback only: the measured STP+CryptoMiniSat characteristic-search run and its x32 allowance (proof Section 6.2).
heuristics.extrapolation: Measured 2^30.03 instructions per CPU-second (callgrind count of a deterministic call against native CPU time) and opcode mix (multiply/divide/floating point 0.42%, unmapped 7.24%) leave 17.0 primitive 256-bit word-RAM operations per instruction at kappa = 2^23 (as in #134), with full sensitivity at 2^24 and 2^25 reported in Section 8.
heuristics.limitations: One single-thread calibration instance; instruction rate under the run's machine load. Enters only the fallback total 2^47.1946370415 for a reviewer who charges the characteristic search (proof Section 6.2).

heuristics.statement: E[C(V,2)] <= q * 2^-5 for the number V of valid tuples in one trial.
heuristics.scope: Valid tuples sharing one first block.
heuristics.extrapolation: 9 within-part pairs in 2^34 part-trials; cross-part term estimated from multiplicity sums with the observed correlation factor; charge exceeds the estimate by more than 20x.

heuristics.statement: The first-block work is the operation count of the explicit straight-line 7-lane batch of proof Section 8 A on the cost model's 256-bit word RAM with 64 registers: 2,047 arithmetic, 71 loads, 30 stores and 101 address operations, plus 24 for entry and exit (16 itemised), per 7 trials. Its 53 simultaneously live values and 8 registers held across the batch fit the 64 registers.
heuristics.scope: Only the register count of the machine on which the first-block batch is charged; every other charge keeps 6e5214dd's model. Lane masks, the 16-word schedule window, the state and the temporaries are registers; M0 is stored for output.
heuristics.extrapolation: The cost model collision-frontier-v5 lists primitive operations and fixes no register count. The promoted blake3-r2 package 52bb50ee states its machine as the 256-bit word RAM of the cost model with 64 registers, and our passed r31 package 028aa8d0 uses the same machine with merged sigma masks and a liveness check. The replay (organizer-executed on submission) runs this program on every seed, compares all seven lanes with scalar C_32, asserts the counts and checks the liveness bound with the 8 persistent registers.
heuristics.limitations: A reviewer who holds the batch to 6e5214dd's register use (masks resident, schedule words and W reloaded) gets a 2,575-operation batch and the total 2^40.714717. Liveness counts SSA values of the straight-line batch; register allocation itself is not executed.

heuristics.statement: The fixed submitted TAB2 has maximum bucket occupancy at most 936 (27-bit buckets, hence also its 32-bit-bucket refinement). For the counterfactual uncapped counted Step-2/3 work demand X of one independent uniform first-block trial under the 2^32-bucket scan, the lazy CV1[1..7] extraction and the seven-lane stage-16/17 sweep with scalar re-run of stage-17 survivors, E[X] <= 92.923, E[X^2] <= 4.2301e12 and 0 <= X <= 435,642,196,448; one-sided Bernstein bounds the probability that the total exceeds 96.2 T by less than 1.3145e-4.
heuristics.scope: The Step-2/3 work counter in proof Section 8 and its hard cap W_cap = 96.2 T for T = 7,832,802,607,654 independent uniform first-block trials; the lazy extraction is charged once per nonempty-bucket trial.
heuristics.extrapolation: The inherited full-table participant enumeration reports exact maximum bucket occupancy 936, and the fixed builder asserts that bound before prefix construction. The mean combines the 2^32-bucket mean occupancy N/2^32 < 0.32522 (uniform key; it also bounds the nonempty-bucket probability, which carries the 56-operation lazy extraction), Step-2 pass fractions, q upper confidence bound, and per-candidate Step-3 work 8.832844 = 11*28092/196608 + 7*f16*57*28092/196608 + 7*f17*25*28092/196608 + f17*2354 with f16 <= 0.126 and f17 <= 2^-14.9, the pack-level stage-16 pass bounded by the union bound 7 f16 (no new premise). The seven-lane decisions equal a full-equation scalar reference on 49,545,216 lane decisions plus 279,946 targeted ones (proof Section 8.3). E[X] <= 5(0.32522) + 56(0.32522) + 0.32522(192) + q_UCB(600 + 196,608 x 8.832844) < 92.923. Worst case S3_max = 600 + 28092*93 + 196608*2354 = 465,428,388 gives support M = 5*936 + 56 + 936(1304 + S3_max) = 435,642,196,448; Bernstein at excess 3.277 T gives exp(-8.9369893) < 1.3145e-4, subtracted in full.
heuristics.limitations: The rates, moments and maximum occupancy are participant measurements rather than organizer full-table executions; the bound assumes the claimed random first-block trials transfer those distributions independently and inherits the unobserved cross-part tuple-pair premise. If the fixed table has a bucket above 936, the builder aborts and the success claim fails rather than using the Bernstein bound.

heuristics.statement: The finite no-sort P1-P4 reference pseudocode, with TAB2 bucketed by all 32 bits of A[-1] and PC-4's w7-independent predicates hoisted to the LEFT row, requires at most 51,230,791,107,584 primitive word operations, plus 25,178,112 for the lane-packed P4 copy and its R1 assertion, i.e. at most 23,035,438,979 target-compression units; the integer ceiling is charged.
heuristics.scope: The one-time 32-bit-bucket TAB2 and P4 construction charged as term C in proof Section 8, including both W7 passes, record actions, fixed-array administration, bucket zeroing/prefix/cursor checks and auxiliary rows.
heuristics.extrapolation: Static worst-case source audit: the exact PC-1 L4, PC-1 L7, PC-2, PC-3, two-pass PC-4 and PC-5 loop counts are charged their displayed per-iteration maxima 2,096, 3,312, 7,280, 3,760, 3,872 per LEFT row plus 32 per (row, w7) pair, and 6,256, respectively, totaling 41,630,497,558,528 main-loop operations. PC-4 is itemised (this version): AeqP(3,3), EeqP(7,7) and the sigma0 cancellation do not depend on w7 (rows A3, A[-1] and E3 carry no difference, and W7' - W7 = D(W7) for every w7 in L7), fix(A,-1) is empty and P3_w7_conditions is empty, so they are charged per LEFT row and pass at the old full body 3,872, and the remaining per-(row, w7) body at 32 (10 itemised); the replay checks the identities on organizer-seeded rows. Every W7 candidate in one complete pass receives a separate 64-operation record-action charge; each of the 2^32+1 bucket boundaries (2^27+1 in the audited layout plus 2^32-2^27 added by d8d39011) receives 1,024 operations covering both count/cursor and offset arrays, including the maximum-occupancy assertion; and every retained auxiliary row receives another 1,024 operations. The exact integer sum is divided by C=2224 and rounded upward to 23,035,427,657; the lane-packed P4 copy (196,608 rows at 128 operations, including the R1 identity assertion) and per-group broadcasts (12 x 1,024) add 11,322 units, for 23,035,438,979.
heuristics.limitations: The exact table cardinalities are inherited participant enumerations from #26/#296. The audit is for the displayed prospective fixed-capacity, no-sort word-RAM pseudocode; it is not a compilable historical source file, native instruction trace, wall-time measurement or organizer full build. Different predicates, capacities, dynamic growth or sorting invalidate the bound.

heuristics.statement: The fixed starting solution used by this algorithm is the single Step-1 solution used by S to build its TAB2 and published collision pair; S reports about 2^34.3 for finding that solution, and the submitted D = 2^35 = 34,359,738,368 target-compression units covers construction of this exact fixed advice.
heuristics.scope: Construction of the exact fixed values A4..A13, E8..E13, W12 and W13 used by P1-P4/TAB2 and the inherited cardinality, rate and work measurements; no substitution of another SAT output.
heuristics.extrapolation: S Sect. 4 first finds one valid through-step-13 solution, fixes the listed state/message words based on it, builds TAB2 and reports about 2^34.3 for finding the Step-1 solution. If that unstated unit is a full 35-step compression, conversion by 2476/2224 gives ceil(2^34.3 x 2476/2224) = 23,547,494,749 < 2^35, leaving a factor 1.459. The two local 908.8-CPU-second alternate-solution runs corroborate task scale only and are not used for transfer.
heuristics.limitations: The historical Step-1 execution was not independently reproduced and S reports only about 2^34.3 without stating its unit or providing a trace. The 1.459 conversion margin therefore remains heuristic. The locally generated solutions differ from T and do not establish interchangeability; the scored algorithm uses only T.

heuristics.statement: The characteristic and starting-solution searches need at most 2^33 bytes at peak.
heuristics.scope: Memory of the characteristic and starting-solution searches, which run before the attack phase.
heuristics.extrapolation: Measured peak resident set 5.25 GiB over all 59 characteristic-search calls and the two corroborative starting-solution runs; S's historical starting-solution run is assumed not to exceed the same 2^33-byte envelope.
heuristics.limitations: S's historical peak is not reported; the measured peaks are added to the memory bound anyway.
